response.strategies:
Shape and shade changes randomly so I want to choose items with same shape and shade. Or at least I try not to choose three different colors with three different shapes. 
texture does not matter that much as it follows a order. But I try to choose stripes/dots, as similar distance to plain or stripes/dots
response.achievement_strategies:
sometimes, I confused about actor and recipient so if there was an item completed, I tried to not touch it.
I started with identifying what features do I need to achieve goals and want to make sure I do not lose them.
response.instruction_feedback: At beginning, I thought it was required that the goals should be different in colors and shapes. After a few trials, I realized that people can choose three identical ones or at least two identical ones?
response.improvement: fewer trials? It was an interesting task, but still I lost interest after maybe 15 trials?
response.feedback: On the debrief page, I think the slider does not match with the scores.

stimulus:
Goal Selection Study Debrief

Thank you for your participation in our research study.

Much research shows that goals change how people learn and make decisions. This study examines how people choose their own goals, and then make decisions in order to achieve those goals.

If you are interested in reading some research about this topic, here are two references:

  • Molinaro, G., & Collins, A. G. E. (2023). A goal-centric outlook on learning. Trends in Cognitive Sciences. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tics.2023.08.011
  • Chu, J., Tenenbaum, J. B., & Schulz, L. E. (2024). In praise of folly: Flexible goals and human cognition. Trends in Cognitive Sciences, 28(7), 628-642. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tics.2024.03.006

If you have any questions or comments, please do not hesitate to ask us. Thank you for your participation.
